act-mwater-backup-restore-check.what: an Evidence comment on the Asana task
act-mwater-backup-restore-check.summary:
Form 0ac68d8274d24f54af0c28b29119b77d, "Piped Water || Water Quality Testing_ SDWS 3__ Result", carries the "Fer > 0.2 mg/l" calculation (36d19995…). mWater restored this form on 23 Sep (John Feighery, "Re: Piped Water survey"). It was repaired to rev 116 the same day. It is now at rev 120 (build snapshot of 5 Oct; the MCP does not report the revision). No email gives the backup date or the revision it was restored to.

The 26 and 27 Sep "replies from mWater support" are mWater's daily unread reminders. They quote Lanja's own message: "it was the calculation Fer > 0.2 mg/l who was the problem. I tried the backup and it works fine now". That means MadAvance's organisational backup runs again. It does not mean a form was restored from a backup.

Nothing was lost. Checked read-only on 6 Oct against our rev 110 copy (16 Sep) and the snapshots at rev 116, 119 and 120. All 22 questions, their choices, the Temperature and pH validations, the French text on 1.2.1–1.2.3 and all 17 calculations are present.

- "Fer > 0.2 mg/l" had no condition at rev 109 and 110 (when: null). It now reads "If Iron > 0.2 Then 1 Else 0", as its label says.
- The Malagasy locale on Entretien préventif (de26d89a, rev 502 since 21 Sep, locales en and fr) was never added, so it was not lost. That is still act-mwater-mg-locale.
- The SDWS 3 operating-status question (OPSTATUS) was added on 29 Sep, after the restore, on the sampling form 43c96af4. It is present live.
- None of the 13 snapshot forms changed revision between 26 and 28 Sep.

Full write-up: Central Data Hub - Water Documents/Evidence/mWater/form-restore-check-2026-10-06.md

act-run-sdws-26-premises.what: the finding that the November 2025 round had already run, logged in data/decisions.json
act-run-sdws-26-premises.summary: Superseded, not abandoned. The premise was that SDWS 26 had no field instrument and no data until a new round ran. Both were false: the annual monitoring survey (form 2eeb8682) already carried the usage question in both seasons and had been run 11-21 November 2025, giving 410 responses that answered both seasons. The parameter is measured for the 2025 monitoring period. Replaced by act-sdws26-annual-round, which makes it a recurring annual obligation rather than a one-off, and by act-sdws26-approve-2025 for the approval state.

act-sdws18-james-rulings.what: written reply from James answering (a) and (b)
act-sdws18-james-rulings.source: James Walker, "Re: Water program dashboard & actions", 1 Oct 2026 09:33 UTC
act-sdws18-james-rulings.summary: (a) The six-month rule counts per pump from its installation or rehabilitation date, and applies in every annual round. (b) Kit and SOP details should be on file; no paired pump sample is needed under methodology v1.0.

act-sdws26-instrument-review.what: the same finding, logged in data/decisions.json
act-sdws26-instrument-review.summary: Superseded. The review was scoped to sign an instrument off BEFORE round one, and round one had already run - on the annual monitoring survey, not on the point-of-use form the review was written against. The substance is not lost: which form is the standing SDWS 26 instrument, and whether it must also carry SDWS 22 boiling, the JMP core questions, the enumerator's identity and the household-versus-institution split, is carried into act-sdws26-annual-round as the question to settle before the 2026 round.

act-sdws27-basis.what: Gold Standard's written answer to the five SDWS 27 questions, forwarded by James Walker
act-sdws27-basis.source: email “Re: Water program dashboard & actions” from James Walker, 2026-09-21
act-sdws27-basis.summary: Capped at 347 days without a sensor; actual days claimable only for sensor-fitted pumps, sampled 50 per stratum, with the cap on the rest; a lost or damaged calendar is acceptable given the SOP, visits and call log. James Walker's ruling, not Gold Standard's.

act-sensor-sample.what: Adriaan's confirmation that the brief was given
act-sensor-sample.summary: Done: Ralf van Veenendaal (Curtech) was briefed on the fleet-wide unit count and the calibration sample by WhatsApp.

act-settle-baseline-boiling-device.what: James Walker's written ruling on the baseline boiling device for stove-holding households
act-settle-baseline-boiling-device.source: email “Re: Water program dashboard & actions” from James Walker, 2026-09-18
act-settle-baseline-boiling-device.summary: The ex post figures are adjusted by the share of end users reporting an improved cookstove in the annual monitoring; Fort-Dauphin 2025: 81%.

act-standardised-stroke-test-basis.what: the basis settled on 18 September 2026, logged in data/decisions.json
act-standardised-stroke-test-basis.source: email “Re: Water program dashboard & actions”, 18 September 2026
act-standardised-stroke-test-basis.summary: Yes. The standardised stroke test is SDWS 28 of ERSDWS V2, and the five-minute test is the accepted method pending the StrokeMeter.
